skill.name: blackforge
skill.description: Answer crypto spot market questions through BlackForge MCP tools or its CLI, with metric definitions, historical comparisons, and data quality context.
skill.summary: Query and explain crypto spot market measurements through BlackForge MCP tools or its CLI.
skill.author: blackforge-so

security_audit.summary: The static alerts reflect documentation syntax, market vocabulary, public catalog access, and intended authentication rather than demonstrated malicious behavior. Two semantic risks remain: automatic execution of unpinned npm clients and credential exposure through documented command arguments. No evidence found of prompt injection, deliberate credential theft, or unrelated sensitive-file access in the reviewed sources.

remediation.issue: The fallback and MCP configuration execute unpinned npm packages without an explicit installation approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed client versions, verify package integrity, and require user approval before downloading or executing a missing client. Prefer an existing reviewed installation.

remediation.issue: Setup examples encourage placing API credentials directly in command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Use an interactive hidden-input credential prompt or a supported secret manager instead of literal keys in commands. Keep credential files private and outside version control.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Execution of Unpinned External Clients
semantic_findings.description: The wrapper falls back to "npx -y @blackforge-so/cli", and the plugin launches an unpinned MCP package. A compromised release could execute with user privileges and access available credentials. No evidence found that these packages are malicious; their implementations are outside this source review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback directly executes an unversioned package with automatic confirmation. The plugin uses the same mechanism, establishing supply-chain exposure without proving malicious intent.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Exposure Through Setup Command Arguments
semantic_findings.description: The setup commands place "BLACKFORGE_API_KEY=bf_your_key_here" and "blackforge auth set-key bf_your_key_here" directly in arguments. Replacing these placeholders with real keys can expose credentials through shell history and process inspection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented workflow requires substituting real credentials into command arguments. Exposure depends on local history and process visibility; the repository itself contains only placeholders.

content.user_title: Explore Crypto Market Data with BlackForge
content.value_statement: Crypto market questions require precise metric definitions, exchange identifiers, and reliable time windows. BlackForge connects those questions to its MCP tools or CLI and explains returned measurements with units and quality context.
actual_capabilities: Discover exchange identifiers, metric definitions, units, and plan requirements through the public BlackForge catalog.
List available trading pairs using each exchange's native symbol format.
Retrieve the latest completed market snapshot with selected columns and quality flags.
Retrieve metric time series and derive bid-ask spreads from matching best bid and best ask timestamps.
Explain liquidity, trade flow, trade timing, and enrichment measurements using documented units and quality context.
Report account usage, remaining monthly rows, omitted columns, and plan restrictions.
limitations: Requires a configured BlackForge MCP server or CLI and an API key for authenticated queries.
Available venues, columns, history, and intervals depend on the API key's plan and remaining quota.
Reads completed windows only; it does not operate live formulas, notifications, or order execution.
Provides measurements rather than trading recommendations; external client implementations and service coverage are not bundled.

use_cases.title: Review Spot Market Liquidity
use_cases.description: Inspect resting liquidity and taker volume for a specified pair, with clear units, snapshot timing, and data quality caveats.

use_cases.title: Compare Historical Measurements
use_cases.description: Retrieve aligned time series and compare measured spreads or trade flow across periods without treating observations as forecasts.

use_cases.title: Check Data Access and Consumption
use_cases.description: Confirm available pairs, account usage, and plan restrictions before integrating BlackForge measurements into a reporting workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Find Available Pairs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use BlackForge to list Kraken pairs quoted in USDT. Confirm exchange and symbol identifiers before presenting the results.

prompt_templates.title: Read a Latest Snapshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the latest ETHUSDT bid depth within 5% on Binance. Include units, quality flags, and the actual completed bucket length.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: retrieve and interpret one measurement.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Taker Trade Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare SOLUSDT taker buy and sell volume on Binance over the last 24 hours. State the UTC range, supported interval, and quality caveats.

prompt_templates.title: Derive a Historical Spread
prompt_templates.prompt: Derive BTC-USDT bid-ask spreads on OKX for the last seven days from best bid and ask series. Align timestamps and report plan restrictions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: derive a measurement from aligned series.

output_examples.input: Explain ETHUSDT bid depth within 5% on Binance.
output_examples.output: Example interpretation: this value measures resting buy liquidity from the best bid down to 5% below it, in USDT. The result includes the completed bucket time and relevant quality flags.

output_examples.input: Show the BTC-USDT spread on OKX over the last week.
output_examples.output: Example interpretation: spread equals best ask minus best bid at matching timestamps. The comparison states the UTC range, selected interval, and any missing points or quality concerns.

output_examples.input: Why is my historical series shorter than requested?
output_examples.output: Example explanation: your plan may limit how far back the key can read. Compare the first returned timestamp with the requested start before concluding that older data is unavailable.

best_practices: Confirm metric keys and native exchange symbols through the catalog and pair list before querying.
Include quality flags, units, UTC timestamps, and the actual plan-supported interval when reporting measurements.
Use reviewed, version-pinned clients and keep API credentials outside command arguments, shared configuration, and version control.
anti_patterns: Treating resting liquidity, trade flow, or historical spreads as buy or sell recommendations.
Guessing metric keys, confusing percent depth bands with basis points, or requesting non-queryable identity fields.
Interpreting omitted columns or silently shortened history as proof that the underlying data does not exist.

faq.question: What must I configure before querying data?
faq.answer: Configure the BlackForge MCP server or CLI and provide an API key for authenticated queries. The public catalog does not require a key.

faq.question: Does this skill recommend trades?
faq.answer: No. It explains measured market data and does not provide buy or sell recommendations or execute orders.

faq.question: Which exchanges does the skill describe?
faq.answer: The documentation lists Binance, Bitget, Bybit, Coinbase, Gate, Kraken, KuCoin, MEXC, and OKX. Confirm current availability and plan access through the catalog.

faq.question: How current is the latest snapshot?
faq.answer: It is the latest completed bucket at your plan's granularity: five minutes for Max or Ultra, one hour for Pro, and one day for Free.

faq.question: Why can columns or historical points be missing?
faq.answer: Plans can omit restricted columns and silently shorten readable history. Compare returned timestamps with your requested range and inspect accounting headers when available.

faq.question: Can the skill calculate a bid-ask spread?
faq.answer: Yes. There is no dedicated spread metric, so it subtracts best bid from best ask using matching time-series timestamps.
